To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in the SHR the VP mRNA levels are elevated in the SON and the PVN, while the OT mRNA levels are lower in the SON and in the PVN.

in the spontaneously hypertensive rats VP mRNA levels are increased, and OT mRNA levels are decreased in the hypothalamic nuclei of the VP-OT system, while pituitary contents of VP and OT are increased and VP plasma levels are elevated.
the hypothalamic VP and OT systems of the SHR are differently regulated in early and late development of hypertension.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the hypothalamo-hypophyseal neurosecretory system in relation to the pathophysiology of hypertension.
the development of a novel approach to the development of the hypothalamo-hypophyseal system.
the role of the hypothalamus in blood pressure regulation and with the role of vasopressin in the pathophysiology of essential hypertension.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in the SHR VP and OT systems are differently regulated during the development of hypertension.
the SHR exhibits a hyperactivity of the VP system in relation to OT.
the VP system is upregulated in the SHR, while the OT-system is downregulated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the VP system is activated early in the development of hypertension in the SHR, and that this activation persists during the course of the disease.
the VP and OT gene expression is regulated in a different manner in SHR and WKY and that this regulation may be involved in the development of hypertension in the SHR.
in SHR the hypothalamic VP system is in an activated state, whereas the OT system is in an inhibited state.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the VP system is more active in the SHR than the OT system, and the VP system is activated before the development of hypertension.
there is a difference in the expression of VP and OT mRNA in the SHR, which may be due to a difference in the activity of the VP and OT systems.
the VP system is already hyperactive in 4-week-old animals.
